Task counted as solved if at least one of the independent baseliners succeeded, over METR's 773 human runs on 188 of the 228 tasks, weighted exactly as Epoch's average_score (invsqrt task weights) so the figure sits on the ingested metric. Each attempt is a distinct person (HCAST: one baseliner per task, screened by qualification tasks, degree from a top-100 university or 3+ years of relevant experience; SWAA: 3 to 4 METR employees per task; RE-Bench: the RE-Bench expert pool). Attempts per task range from 1 to 69 and METR collected more of them where baselines failed, so the committee lift lands mostly on the hard tasks and the sparsely baselined ones stay near their single-attempt value; a fixed best-of-3 gives 0.80 for reference. Under the same best-of-N rule the models rise too: Claude Opus 4.6 reaches 0.886 against 0.825 for its mean on these tasks. User decision 2026-09-11.
